column1: # Reviewed replacement for the hand-typed NMAP_RAW / MINMAP dictionaries at
# Those two literals decide the identity of 268,697 component records -- 40.4% of
# the corpus -- and every one of them was stamped mapping_confidence "exact" with
# no structure consulted anywhere in either script.
# This table states, per nutrient, what the USDA measurement actually is, what BiGG
# id it maps to, and what evidence tier that mapping can honestly claim. It is the
# reviewed artefact the builder should read instead of a literal, so a rebuild
# HANDOFF: `usda_nutrient_number` is deliberately EMPTY. FoodData Central nutrient
# numbers are the correct key (the display name is not stable and collides -- see
# the five collision groups below), but the USDA input archives referenced at
# build_usda_media_v2.py:11-13 point at a deleted scratchpad and are not on this
# host, so the numbers cannot be read from the source. They must be filled in when
# the USDA input is restored. They are left blank rather than guessed.
# COLLISIONS (five groups where two USDA nutrients resolve to one exchange and the
# builder's `comps[ex] = {...}` assignment lets the second silently overwrite the
# first): Cystine/Cysteine -> cys__L; MUFA 18:1 c + MUFA 18:1 -> ocdcea;
# PUFA 18:2 n-6 c,c + PUFA 18:2 c -> lnlc; PUFA 18:3 n-3 c,c,c (ALA) + PUFA 18:3 c
# -> lnlnca; PUFA 20:4 + PUFA 20:4c -> arachd. The builder must assert that no two
# source nutrients resolve to one exchange within a food and record both amounts.
# BUILD GATE: tools/build_usda_media_v2.py:32,35 currently filter the table with
# `{k: v for k, v in NMAP_RAW.items() if valid(v)}`, which DROPS any entry whose
# target is not in_biggr with no log line. That silent drop must become a hard
# build failure naming the entry, or a correction like "Cystine -> cystine__L"
# deletes the nutrient instead of fixing it.

column8: USDA amino-acid profiles are protein hydrolysates; the proteinogenic L-form is the correct assignment.

L-cystine is the disulfide DIMER, C6H12N2O4S2, InChIKey LEVWYRKDKASIDU-IMJSIDKUSA-N, BiGG id cysi__L (in_biggr true). It was mapped to cys__L, the L-cysteine MONOMER, C3H7NO2S, XUJNEKJLAYXESH-REOHCLBHSA-N: different skeleton, 2x stoichiometry. Retarget to cysi__L, NOT to cystine__L (which is in_biggr false with no formula and no InChIKey and would be silently dropped by the valid() filter).
Correct on its own, but shares the exchange key with Cystine; whichever nutrient is parsed second overwrites the first amount with no trace.
conjugate-base naming; asp__L is L-aspartate, the same species at physiological pH
a saturated straight-chain fatty acid of stated length is unambiguous
cis-C18:1 without a stated double-bond position. BiGG resolves six C18:1 species; oleate is assumed and must be declared as a proxy.
Total C18:1 including trans isomers. Also collides with "MUFA 18:1 c" on the same exchange.
position and geometry both stated; linoleate is the specific compound
cis-C18:2 without a stated position. No isomer-unresolved C18:2 target exists (ocdcya duplicates lnlc's InChIKey), so lnlc stays as a declared proxy.
position and geometry both stated; alpha-linolenate
C20:4 without a stated position; arachidonate assumed
synonym naming: nac is nicotinate. USDA "Niacin" excludes nicotinamide (reported separately), so the assignment is defensible.
conjugate-base naming; the R enantiomer is the vitamer
USDA reports total B6 across pyridoxine, pyridoxal, pyridoxamine and their 5'-phosphates. pydxn is pyridoxine alone.
total food folates (largely polyglutamyl 5-methyl-THF) plus added folic acid, mapped to folate monoglutamate

cbl1 is Cob(I)alamin, a transient reduced intracellular redox state, not a dietary species. Cyanocobalamin has no in_biggr id (b12 has no formula and no InChIKey). adocbl is a real dietary/coenzyme form present in BiGGr; declare it a proxy for the vitamer group.
conjugate-base naming; ascb__L is L-ascorbate. USDA totals ascorbic + dehydroascorbic acid, so an aggregate note is warranted but the species is right.
reported as alpha-tocopherol equivalents in many records
totals free choline, phosphocholine, glycerophosphocholine, phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin
monatomic ion; the element assay and the BiGG species are the same entity
total P includes phytate, phospholipid and protein-bound P, not only free orthophosphate. Not flux-consequential: the mineral base already opens EX_pi_e at -1000.

total Fe is mixed heme/non-heme and mixed oxidation state; fe2 fixes Fe(II) and its BiGG display name is "Fe2+ mitochondria". Not flux-consequential: the mineral base already opens both EX_fe2_e and EX_fe3_e at -1000.
an elemental Mo assay mapped to molybdate. Flux-consequential: molybdate is not in the injected mineral base.

an elemental Se assay mapped to selenite. Dietary Se is predominantly selenomethionine/selenocysteine. Flux-consequential: selenite is not in the injected mineral base and is opened at lower_bound -1000.
